title: Processor architecture specification
description: Schema for architecture-level spec files in docs/specs/common/arch/. An architecture spec captures metadata that is identical on every device implementing that processor architecture: word size, endianness, pipeline configuration, the full architectural memory map, the exception model (vector table layout, exception stack frame, EXC_RETURN values, exception table), and settings encodings shared by all devices of that architecture.

spec-version.description: Spec format version using semantic versioning (semver), e.g. '1.0.0'. Increment the patch version for corrections, the minor version for backward-compatible additions, and the major version for breaking changes.

pipeline-type.description: Pipeline memory architecture (Harvard separates instruction and data buses; Von Neumann shares them).

address-space.description: Total addressable memory space in bits (e.g. 32 for a 4GB address space).

memory.description: Architecture-defined memory regions (e.g. Private Peripheral Bus). These regions are identical on every device implementing this architecture.

note.description: Optional free-text annotation for the architecture memory section.

definitions.description: Reusable definitions shared across all devices of this architecture. Values are referenced via YAML anchors/aliases in family specs.

settings.description: Named settings maps that are architecturally defined and identical across all devices. Keys are settings-block names; values are the bit-pattern-to-description mappings.

exceptions.description: Architecturally-defined exception model. Exception numbers, vector offsets, EXC_RETURN values, and the exception stack frame are identical on every device implementing this architecture.

stack-frame.description: Register state saved on the active stack at exception entry.

exc-return.description: Valid EXC_RETURN values. Loading one of these into PC from an exception handler triggers exception return.

entries.description: Architectural exception table. Exception numbers, vector offsets, and fixed priorities are identical on every device implementing this architecture.

hex-address.description: A hex address or byte offset (e.g. 0x40000000). Written in hex notation in the source YAML; parsed as an integer by most YAML parsers.

settings.description: Enumerated bit-pattern settings for a field. Keys are binary bit patterns (e.g. '00', '10', '1111'). Null means no settings are documented.

memory-type.description: ARMv6-M architectural memory type for this region (PM0223 Table 4).

xn.description: Execute Never. true means instruction fetches from this region generate a HardFault.

shareability.description: ARMv6-M architectural shareability attribute (PM0223 Table 4). Omit when not constrained by the architecture.

cache-policy.description: ARMv6-M architectural cache policy (PM0223 Table 4). WT=write-through no write-allocate; WBWA=write-back write-allocate. Omit when not applicable (Device or Strongly-ordered regions).

note.description: Optional free-text annotation for constraints not expressible as formal properties.

arch-vector-table.description: Architectural vector table properties identical on every device implementing this architecture.

reset-address.description: Address of the vector table at reset.

alignment-bytes.description: Minimum alignment of the vector table in bytes. VTOR bits below log2(alignment) are always zero.

entry-size-bytes.description: Size of each vector table entry in bytes.

lsb-must-be-set.description: true if bit[0] of each exception vector entry must be 1 to indicate Thumb code.

arch-exception-stack-frame.description: Register state pushed onto the active stack by the processor on exception entry.

words.description: Number of 32-bit words pushed onto the active stack on exception entry.

alignment-bytes.description: Stack pointer alignment enforced on exception entry.

layout.description: Stack frame fields in order from lowest to highest address.

offset.description: Byte offset from the stack pointer value at exception entry.

field.description: Register or processor state saved at this offset.

arch-exc-return.description: A valid EXC_RETURN value written to LR on exception entry. Loading this value into PC triggers the exception return sequence.

value.description: 32-bit EXC_RETURN magic value (bits[31:4] are 0xFFFFFFF on ARMv6-M).

return-to.description: Processor mode entered after exception return.

stack.description: Stack pointer used to restore state on exception return.

arch-exception.description: An architecturally-defined exception. Reserved ranges and IRQ blocks may use range strings for number, irq, and vector-offset.

number.description: Exception number (1-based). May be a range string (e.g. '4-10') for reserved or IRQ blocks.

irq.description: CMSIS IRQ number. Negative for system exceptions, 0-based for external IRQs, null if not applicable. May be a range string for IRQ blocks.

vector-offset.description: Byte offset of the exception vector from the vector table base. May be a range string for blocks (e.g. '0x00000040-0x000000BC').

fixed-priority.description: Fixed exception priority (negative integer for Reset/NMI/HardFault). null for configurable-priority or reserved exceptions.

configurable-priority.description: true if software can configure the priority of this exception via NVIC or system handler priority registers.

activation.description: How the exception is raised: synchronous (caused by instruction) or asynchronous (external signal or software-pended).
